title: Best Dehumidifier for Sleeping (2026): Quiet Bedroom Picks
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for Sleeping: Quiet Picks for a Drier Bedroom
dek: Sticky sheets and a muggy bedroom make for restless nights. These dehumidifiers dry the air without a racket — and switch off before the room gets too dry.
description: The best dehumidifier for sleeping, chosen for low noise, sleep modes and accurate humidistats, plus whether it’s safe and healthy to sleep with one on.
intro: Humid air makes a bedroom feel warmer than the thermostat says, keeps sweat from evaporating and gives dust mites and mildew exactly what they want. A **dehumidifier for sleeping** fixes all three, but only if it’s quiet enough that you don’t trade a muggy room for a noisy one.

That narrows the field. The best bedroom units combine a low-noise fan, a sleep mode that dims the display, and a humidistat that stops at a comfortable number instead of drying the air until your throat is scratchy. We picked the models that do that best, from a compressor unit with standout noise ratings to near-silent minis for small rooms, and answered the most common questions about sleeping with a dehumidifier.
topPicksLead: For most bedrooms, the **Midea Cube 20** is the best dehumidifier for sleeping: Consumer Reports rates it Excellent for noise, and its humidistat holds an exact target all night.

products.name: Midea Cube 20-Pint Smart Dehumidifier (MAD20S1QWT)
pros: Excellent noise rating from Consumer Reports
Big base tank rarely fills overnight
Adjust it from bed with the Wi-Fi app
cons: Compressor cycling is audible to light sleepers
products.whyWeLoveIt: It’s the rare compressor dehumidifier that reviewers and owners alike describe as quiet enough to sleep beside. Set it to 45–50% and it cycles off once the bedroom gets there, instead of running on high all night.
products.performance: It’s rated at 20 pints a day under the 2019 DOE test, which is plenty for a closed-door bedroom. Consumer Reports gives it Excellent marks for noise, water removal and humidistat accuracy, and Midea lists it at 42 dB. The tank sits in the base and holds far more than a standard bucket, so you’re unlikely to be woken by a full-tank shutoff. It also carries ENERGY STAR’s Most Efficient designation.

specs.Best for: Bedrooms up to a primary suite

products.name: Midea 22-Pint ENERGY STAR Dehumidifier (MAD22C1AWS)
pros: Lighter and easier to move than a 50-pint unit
cons: Smaller bucket fills quickly in humid weeks
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you want a compressor unit’s real drying power for less than the Cube costs, this conventional Midea box gets you a set-a-number humidistat and ENERGY STAR efficiency at a friendlier price.
products.performance: It’s rated at 22 pints a day under the 2019 DOE test — older labeling would have called it a 35-pint unit — and it’s ENERGY STAR certified, which helps when it runs every night through summer. For a moderately damp bedroom, it holds a set humidity without fuss. Empty the bucket before bed in very humid weeks so a full-tank stop doesn’t let the room creep back up overnight.

products.name: TCL 20-Pint Dehumidifier (TDW20E20)
pros: Rated as low as 49 dB on its lowest fan speed
products.whyWeLoveIt: The 24-hour timer is a sleeper feature. Run it hard for a couple of hours before bed to bring the room down, then let it shut off so there’s no compressor noise while you sleep.
products.performance: TCL rates it for roughly 1,500 square feet and lists noise from 49 dB on its lowest fan speed. The 7.4-pint bucket shuts the unit off when full, so in a muggy room you’ll be emptying it daily. Owner reviews generally describe it as a quiet, dependable single-room machine. See more in our [best TCL dehumidifier](/best/best-tcl-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.whyWeLoveIt: For light sleepers, the problem with compressor units isn’t the steady hum — it’s the click and surge when the compressor kicks on. This thermoelectric mini runs at one even, low level all night.

That keeps a small bedroom or nursery from feeling clammy, but it won’t rescue a genuinely damp room. Compare it with other small units in our [best mini dehumidifier](/best/best-mini-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: Eva-Dry EDV-2400 Dehumidifier with Humidistat
products.award: Best quiet mini with a humidistat

products.whyWeLoveIt: It pairs thermoelectric quiet with something most minis lack: a humidistat. That means it stops when the room is comfortable rather than running all night, which matters if you also want to avoid waking up with a dry throat.
products.performance: It’s Eva-Dry’s step-up electric model, with more airflow and a larger tank than the EDV-1100. Like every Peltier unit, it pulls water most effectively in warm, humid air, so it’s best in summer bedrooms that run warm. If the room still feels damp with it running, you need a 20-pint compressor unit instead.

blocks.text: Most people sleep best toward the middle of that humidity range, around 40–50%. No compressor dehumidifier hits 30 dB, which is why distance from the bed and a well-timed humidistat matter as much as the noise rating. More on the allergy angle in our [dust mite dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-dust-mites/) guide.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for sleeping

blocks.text: We don’t run a sound lab. We compare manufacturer decibel ratings and independent published ratings, such as Consumer Reports’ noise and humidistat-accuracy scores, alongside DOE 2019 capacity, ENERGY STAR listings and manuals for sleep modes, timers and display settings.

Owner reviews carry extra weight for this guide, because they reveal what spec sheets don’t: bright LEDs that can’t be dimmed, full-tank beeps at 3 a.m., and compressors that rattle when they cycle on.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier for sleeping

items.label: Low noise, at the setting you’ll use
items.text: Compare decibel ratings on low fan speed, and remember compressor units also make a brief noise when they cycle on. See our [quiet dehumidifier](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/) picks for more.

items.label: A sleep mode or dimmable display
items.text: A glowing panel can be as disruptive as the fan. Sleep modes typically slow the fan and dim or switch off the lights.

items.label: A set-percentage humidistat
items.text: Set 45–50% so the unit idles once the room is comfortable rather than over-drying it overnight.

items.label: A tank that lasts the night
items.text: A unit that shuts off at 2 a.m. lets humidity creep back. Bigger tanks or a drain hose prevent that.

items.label: The right size for the room
items.text: A 20–22-pint unit suits most bedrooms. An oversized model runs louder than it needs to; an undersized one never stops.

sections.heading: Is it good to sleep with a dehumidifier on?

blocks.text: For most people in a humid climate or a damp room, yes. Drier air lets sweat evaporate, so you feel cooler at the same temperature, and keeping humidity below 50% discourages dust mites and mold — two common triggers for nighttime congestion. Our [allergy dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-allergies/) guide covers that side in depth.

The downsides are manageable. Over-drying can leave you with a dry throat, irritated sinuses or nosebleeds, which is why a humidistat matters. A compressor unit also gives off a little heat; it won’t cool a room, though drier air often feels more comfortable. Our guide on [whether a dehumidifier cools a room](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-cool-a-room/) explains why.

blocks.title: Safety basics
blocks.text: Plug the dehumidifier directly into a wall outlet rather than an extension cord or power strip, leave several inches of clearance on all sides, and keep cords out of walkways where you might trip in the dark.

sections.heading: How to set up a dehumidifier for better sleep

items: **Run it before bed.** Start it an hour or two early with the door closed, so the heavy lifting is done before you lie down.
**Set the humidistat to 45–50%.** Once the room reaches it, the unit idles and the room stays quiet.
**Switch to sleep mode or low fan.** Dim the display, too, if your model allows it.
**Put distance between you and the unit.** Across the room is better than beside the bed; our [placement guide](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) covers clearances.
**Empty the tank at bedtime.** That way a full-tank shutoff won’t let humidity rebound before morning.
**Check with a hygrometer.** A separate reading confirms the room really is in the 40–50% range.

blocks.text: Setting up a baby’s room? See our [nursery dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-nursery/) picks for extra safety considerations.

The **Midea Cube 20** is the best dehumidifier for sleeping for most bedrooms: quiet by published ratings, accurate and efficient. The **Midea 22-Pint** is the value choice, and the **TCL 20-Pint**’s timer lets you dry the room before bed and sleep in silence. Light sleepers in small rooms should consider the compressor-free **Pro Breeze PB-03** or **Eva-Dry EDV-2400**. Whatever you choose, aim for 45–50% — comfortable, not bone-dry. For more room-by-room advice, see our [bedroom dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-bedroom/) guide.

faqs.q: Is it safe to sleep with a dehumidifier on?
faqs.a: Yes. Household dehumidifiers are designed to run unattended. Plug it straight into a wall outlet, keep it clear of bedding and curtains, and use a model with automatic shutoff when the tank is full.

faqs.q: Is sleeping with a dehumidifier good for you?
faqs.a: In a humid room, usually. Keeping humidity around 40–50% helps you feel cooler and limits dust mites and mold. Just don’t let the room drop much below 40%, which can dry out your throat and sinuses.

faqs.q: What humidity is best for sleeping?
faqs.a: Aim for 40–50%. The EPA recommends keeping indoor humidity between 30% and 50%, and the middle of that range is comfortable for most people.

faqs.q: What is the quietest dehumidifier for a bedroom?
faqs.a: Among compressor units, the Midea Cube 20 earns an Excellent noise rating from Consumer Reports. For near-silent running in a small room, a thermoelectric mini like the Pro Breeze PB-03 has no compressor to cycle on and off.

faqs.q: Should I run a dehumidifier all night?
faqs.a: Let the humidistat decide. Set it to 45–50% and the unit will run only when the room rises above that. Or use a timer to dry the room before bed and let it switch off while you sleep.

faqs.q: Where should a dehumidifier go in a bedroom?
faqs.a: On a hard, level floor with several inches of clearance, ideally across the room from the bed and away from curtains. Keep the door closed so it isn’t trying to dry the whole house.
